Why This Matters Erik Wilde: Module 1: Understanding AI-Driven API Usage

(3) Agents Call APIs Autonomously

  • Agents call endpoints, chain services, and generate integrations nobody explicitly designed for
  • The API was written for a developer who reads the docs once and remembers
  • The agent reads the spec every time, and only the spec
  • Every assumption a human would forgive becomes a failure point


Why This Matters Erik Wilde: Module 1: Understanding AI-Driven API Usage

(4) Do Your Developer Experience (DX) Homework

  • Most API descriptions need quality improvements anyway
  • Better descriptions benefit everyone, not just AI agents
    • Complete and meaningful operation summaries
    • Comprehensive examples for all operations
    • Clear error handling
    • Consistent terminology and naming
  • Good DX is the foundation for good agent experience (AX)


Why This Matters Erik Wilde: Module 1: Understanding AI-Driven API Usage

(5) Now There's AX Homework, Too

  • AI agents need information developers don't typically require:
    • Everything that developers usually just know
    • Treat every API like an external one for developers with no context
  • OpenAPI Initiative (OAI) might add AX-specific fields
  • Until then, leverage description fields strategically


Four Ways an API Fails an Agent

Outline (Four Ways an API Fails an Agent)

  1. Why This Matters [3]
  2. Four Ways an API Fails an Agent [4]
  3. Map the Risk [1]
Four Ways an API Fails an Agent Erik Wilde: Module 1: Understanding AI-Driven API Usage

(7) Ambiguity

  • Ambiguity forces an agent to guess. Every guess is a potential failure.
  • Missing descriptions, unclear parameter values, inconsistent field types
  • A human infers from context. An agent has no context beyond the spec.


Four Ways an API Fails an Agent Erik Wilde: Module 1: Understanding AI-Driven API Usage

(8) Unintended Workflows

  • If an agent can do it, it will eventually try it.
  • Endpoints that were never meant to be called in sequence, or called at all
  • An agent doesn't know your intent — only what the spec allows


Four Ways an API Fails an Agent Erik Wilde: Module 1: Understanding AI-Driven API Usage

(9) Missing Information

  • What's not there is often more dangerous than what is.
  • No error responses, no pagination, no security scheme
  • A human asks a colleague. An agent guesses, or fails silently.


Four Ways an API Fails an Agent Erik Wilde: Module 1: Understanding AI-Driven API Usage

(10) Governance Gaps

  • A spec that's hard to govern is a spec that will be misused at scale.
  • Inconsistent naming, mixed conventions, RPC-style endpoints hiding in a resource-based API
  • One agent misusing this is a bug. A thousand agents is a pattern.
